candidate.answerReason: On the real logarithm domain implicit in log_a b, the circumference equation gives log_10(b)=pi log_10(a). Change of base then yields pi.

methods.label: Use circumference and change base
methods.explanation:
The circle connects the two logarithms through circumference \(=2\pi\times\) radius. The requested real logarithm \(\log_a b\) requires \(a>0\), \(a\ne1\), and \(b>0\). These conditions allow the logarithm power rule to give
\[
\log_{10}(a^2)=2\log_{10}a,
\qquad
\log_{10}(b^4)=4\log_{10}b.
\]
Substituting into the circumference formula yields
\[
4\log_{10}b=2\pi\bigl(2\log_{10}a\bigr),
\]
so \(\log_{10}b=\pi\log_{10}a\).

The radius is positive, so \(2\log_{10}a>0\); in particular, \(\log_{10}a\ne0\). We may therefore divide by it and apply change of base:
\[
\log_a b=\frac{\log_{10}b}{\log_{10}a}=\boxed{\pi}.
\]
The answer is choice C.
